rows.question: Please generate a summary of the closing balances at the end of each month for each customer transactions, show the monthly changes and monthly cumulative bank account balances. Ensure that even if a customer has no account activity in a given month, the balance for that month is still included in the output.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_monthly_aggregates AS (
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  date(strftime('%Y', ct.txn_date) || '-' || strftime('%m', ct.txn_date) || '-01') AS month_start_date,
  date(date(strftime('%Y', ct.txn_date) || '-' || strftime('%m', ct.txn_date) || '-01'), '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end_date,
  SUM(ct.txn_amount) AS monthly_net_amount
FROM customer_transactions AS ct
GROUP BY
  ct.customer_id,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER),
  CAST(strftime('%m', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER)
),
customer_transactions_normalized AS (
SELECT
  customer_transactions.customer_id AS customer_id,
  date(customer_transactions.txn_date) AS txn_date,
  CASE
    WHEN lower(customer_transactions.txn_type) IN ('withdrawal', 'withdraw') THEN -1 * customer_transactions.txn_amount
    WHEN lower(customer_transactions.txn_type) IN ('deposit', 'payment', 'credit') THEN customer_transactions.txn_amount
    ELSE customer_transactions.txn_amount
  END AS txn_amount_signed,
  customer_transactions.txn_type AS txn_type,
  rowid AS txn_id
FROM customer_transactions
),
global_month_calendar AS (
SELECT
  CAST(strftime('%Y', month_start) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', month_start) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  strftime('%Y-%m-01', month_start) AS month_start_date,
  -- month_end is last day of the month: take first day of next month minus one day
  date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', month_start), '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end_date,
  CAST((strftime('%Y', month_start) || printf('%02d', CAST(strftime('%m', month_start) AS INTEGER))) AS INTEGER) AS month_seq
FROM (
  -- generate one row per month between min and max txn_date in customer_transactions
  SELECT date(
           strftime('%Y-%m-01', min_txn),
           '+' || (n) || ' months'
         ) AS month_start
  FROM (
    SELECT
      MIN(txn_date) AS min_txn,
      MAX(txn_date) AS max_txn
    FROM customer_transactions
  ) bounds,
  -- generate sequence numbers from 0 up to number of months difference
  (SELECT
     (SELECT CAST(( (strftime('%Y', max_txn) - strftime('%Y', min_txn)) * 12
       + (strftime('%m', max_txn) - strftime('%m', min_txn)) ) AS INTEGER)
      FROM (SELECT MIN(txn_date) AS min_txn, MAX(txn_date) AS max_txn FROM customer_transactions)
     ) AS month_diff
  ),
  -- numbers table using recursive CTE emulation via cross join of small constants
  (SELECT (a.i + b.i*10) AS n
   FROM (SELECT 0 AS i UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4
         UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9) a,
        (SELECT 0 AS i UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4
         UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9) b
  )
  WHERE n <= (
    SELECT CAST(( (strftime('%Y', max_txn) - strftime('%Y', min_txn)) * 12
       + (strftime('%m', max_txn) - strftime('%m', min_txn)) ) AS INTEGER)
    FROM (SELECT MIN(txn_date) AS min_txn, MAX(txn_date) AS max_txn FROM customer_transactions)
  )
)
),
customer_monthly_balance_rows AS (
SELECT
  ca.customer_id,
  gc.year,
  gc.month,
  gc.month_start_date,
  gc.month_end_date,
  -- closing_balance is cumulative sum of monthly_net_amount up to and including this month
  COALESCE((
    SELECT SUM(agg.monthly_net_amount)
    FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg
    JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc2
      ON agg.year = gc2.year AND agg.month = gc2.month
    WHERE agg.customer_id = ca.customer_id
      AND gc2.month_seq <= gc.month_seq
      AND gc2.month_seq >= (
        -- first month_seq for this customer
        SELECT MIN(gc3.month_seq)
        FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg3
        JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc3
          ON agg3.year = gc3.year AND agg3.month = gc3.month
        WHERE agg3.customer_id = ca.customer_id
      )
  ), 0) AS closing_balance,
  -- monthly_change = closing_balance this month - closing_balance previous month
  COALESCE((
    COALESCE((
      SELECT SUM(agg.monthly_net_amount)
      FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg
      JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc2
        ON agg.year = gc2.year AND agg.month = gc2.month
      WHERE agg.customer_id = ca.customer_id
        AND gc2.month_seq <= gc.month_seq
        AND gc2.month_seq >= (
          SELECT MIN(gc3.month_seq)
          FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg3
          JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc3
            ON agg3.year = gc3.year AND agg3.month = gc3.month
          WHERE agg3.customer_id = ca.customer_id
        )
    ), 0)
    -
    COALESCE((
      SELECT SUM(agg.monthly_net_amount)
      FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg
      JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc2
        ON agg.year = gc2.year AND agg.month = gc2.month
      WHERE agg.customer_id = ca.customer_id
        AND gc2.month_seq <= (gc.month_seq - 1)
        AND gc2.month_seq >= (
          SELECT MIN(gc3.month_seq)
          FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg3
          JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc3
            ON agg3.year = gc3.year AND agg3.month = gc3.month
          WHERE agg3.customer_id = ca.customer_id
        )
    ), 0)
  ), 0) AS monthly_change,
  -- cumulative_balance is alias of closing_balance
  COALESCE((
    SELECT SUM(agg.monthly_net_amount)
    FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg
    JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc2
      ON agg.year = gc2.year AND agg.month = gc2.month
    WHERE agg.customer_id = ca.customer_id
      AND gc2.month_seq <= gc.month_seq
      AND gc2.month_seq >= (
        SELECT MIN(gc3.month_seq)
        FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg3
        JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc3
          ON agg3.year = gc3.year AND agg3.month = gc3.month
        WHERE agg3.customer_id = ca.customer_id
      )
  ), 0) AS cumulative_balance
FROM
  (
    -- distinct customers that have aggregates
    SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_monthly_aggregates
  ) AS ca
CROSS JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc
-- restrict calendar to between each customer's first and last month by ensuring month_seq within customer's range
WHERE gc.month_seq BETWEEN
  (
    SELECT MIN(gc_min.month_seq)
    FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg_min
    JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc_min
      ON agg_min.year = gc_min.year AND agg_min.month = gc_min.month
    WHERE agg_min.customer_id = ca.customer_id
  )
  AND
  (
    SELECT MAX(gc_max.month_seq)
    FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg_max
    JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc_max
      ON agg_max.year = gc_max.year AND agg_max.month = gc_max.month
    WHERE agg_max.customer_id = ca.customer_id
  )
)
SELECT
  customer_id,
  year,
  month,
  month_start_date,
  month_end_date,
  closing_balance,
  monthly_change,
  cumulative_balance
FROM customer_monthly_balance_rows
ORDER BY customer_id ASC, year ASC, month ASC

rows.question: For each customer and each month of 2020, first calculate the month-end balance by adding all deposit amounts and subtracting all withdrawal amounts that occurred during that specific month. Then determine which month in 2020 has the highest count of customers with a positive month-end balance and which month has the lowest count. For each of these two months, compute the average month-end balance across all customers and provide the difference between these two averages
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_monthly_aggregates AS (
  SELECT
    ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
    CAST(strftime('%m', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS month,
    SUM(
      CASE
        WHEN ct.txn_type = 'deposit' THEN IFNULL(ct.txn_amount,0)
        WHEN ct.txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN -IFNULL(ct.txn_amount,0)
        ELSE IFNULL(ct.txn_amount,0)
      END
    ) AS monthly_net_amount
  FROM customer_transactions AS ct
  WHERE ct.txn_date BETWEEN '2020-02-12' AND '2020-04-12'
  GROUP BY
    ct.customer_id,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER),
    CAST(strftime('%m', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER)
),
global_month_calendar AS (
  SELECT 2020 AS year, 2 AS month UNION ALL
  SELECT 2020,3 UNION ALL SELECT 2020,4
),
customer_monthly_balance_including_zeros AS (
  SELECT
    c.customer_id AS customer_id,
    printf('%04d-%02d', gc.year, gc.month) AS year_month,
    COALESCE(agg.monthly_net_amount, 0) AS month_end_balance
  FROM
    (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions) c
  CROSS JOIN
    global_month_calendar gc
  LEFT JOIN
    (
      SELECT
        customer_id,
        printf('%04d-%02d', year, month) AS year_month,
        monthly_net_amount
      FROM customer_monthly_aggregates
    ) agg
    ON agg.customer_id = c.customer_id
    AND agg.year_month = printf('%04d-%02d', gc.year, gc.month)
),
monthly_stats AS (
  SELECT year_month,
         SUM(CASE WHEN month_end_balance > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS positive_count,
         AVG(month_end_balance) AS avg_balance
  FROM customer_monthly_balance_including_zeros
  WHERE year_month BETWEEN '2020-02' AND '2020-04'
  GROUP BY year_month
),
max_row AS (
  SELECT year_month, positive_count, avg_balance
  FROM (
    SELECT m.*,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY positive_count DESC, year_month ASC) AS rn
    FROM monthly_stats m
  ) WHERE rn = 1
),
min_row AS (
  SELECT year_month, positive_count, avg_balance
  FROM (
    SELECT m.*,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY positive_count ASC, year_month ASC) AS rn
    FROM monthly_stats m
  ) WHERE rn = 1
)
SELECT
  max_row.year_month AS highest_month,
  max_row.positive_count AS highest_month_positive_customer_count,
  max_row.avg_balance AS highest_month_average_month_end_balance,
  min_row.year_month AS lowest_month,
  min_row.positive_count AS lowest_month_positive_customer_count,
  min_row.avg_balance AS lowest_month_average_month_end_balance,
  (max_row.avg_balance - min_row.avg_balance) AS average_balance_difference
FROM max_row, min_row

rows.question: For each customer, group all deposits and withdrawals by the first day of each month to obtain a monthly net amount, then calculate each month’s closing balance by cumulatively summing these monthly nets. Next, determine the most recent month’s growth rate by comparing its closing balance to the prior month’s balance, treating deposits as positive and withdrawals as negative, and if the previous month’s balance is zero, the growth rate should be the current month’s balance multiplied by 100. Finally, compute the percentage of customers whose most recent month shows a growth rate of more than 5%.

WITH customer_monthly_aggregates AS (
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  date(strftime('%Y', ct.txn_date) || '-' || strftime('%m', ct.txn_date) || '-01') AS month_start_date,
  date(date(strftime('%Y', ct.txn_date) || '-' || strftime('%m', ct.txn_date) || '-01'), '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end_date,
  SUM(ct.txn_amount) AS monthly_net_amount
FROM customer_transactions AS ct
GROUP BY
  ct.customer_id,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER),
  CAST(strftime('%m', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER)
),
customer_monthly_net AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  substr(txn_date, 1, 7) || '-01' AS month_start,
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
      WHEN txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN -txn_amount
      ELSE txn_amount
    END
  ) AS monthly_net_amount
FROM customer_transactions
GROUP BY customer_id, month_start
),
global_month_calendar AS (
SELECT
  CAST(strftime('%Y', month_start) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', month_start) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  strftime('%Y-%m-01', month_start) AS month_start_date,
  -- month_end is last day of the month: take first day of next month minus one day
  date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', month_start), '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end_date,

FROM (
  -- generate one row per month between min and max txn_date in customer_transactions
  SELECT date(
           strftime('%Y-%m-01', min_txn),
           '+' || (n) || ' months'
         ) AS month_start
  FROM (
    SELECT
      MIN(txn_date) AS min_txn,
      MAX(txn_date) AS max_txn
    FROM customer_transactions
  ) bounds,
  -- generate sequence numbers from 0 up to number of months difference
  (SELECT
     (SELECT CAST(( (strftime('%Y', max_txn) - strftime('%Y', min_txn)) * 12
       + (strftime('%m', max_txn) - strftime('%m', min_txn)) ) AS INTEGER)
      FROM (SELECT MIN(txn_date) AS min_txn, MAX(txn_date) AS max_txn FROM customer_transactions)
     ) AS month_diff
  ),
  -- numbers table using recursive CTE emulation via cross join of small constants
  (SELECT (a.i + b.i*10) AS n
   FROM (SELECT 0 AS i UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4
         UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9) a,
        (SELECT 0 AS i UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4
         UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9) b
  )
  WHERE n <= (
    SELECT CAST(( (strftime('%Y', max_txn) - strftime('%Y', min_txn)) * 12
       + (strftime('%m', max_txn) - strftime('%m', min_txn)) ) AS INTEGER)
    FROM (SELECT MIN(txn_date) AS min_txn, MAX(txn_date) AS max_txn FROM customer_transactions)
  )
)
),
clean_customer_transactions AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
  date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(txn_date))) AS txn_month_start,
  lower(txn_type) AS txn_type,
  CASE
    WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN ABS(txn_amount)
    WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'withdrawal' THEN -ABS(txn_amount)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS txn_amount_signed
FROM customer_transactions
WHERE lower(txn_type) IN ('deposit','withdrawal')
),
customer_monthly_closing_balance AS (
SELECT
  cma.customer_id AS customer_id,
  cma.month_start AS month_start,
  -- numeric month ordering to identify prior calendar month relationships
  (CAST(strftime('%Y', cma.month_start) AS INTEGER) * 12 + CAST(strftime('%m', cma.month_start) AS INTEGER)) AS month_order,
  cma.monthly_net_amount AS monthly_net_amount,
  -- running sum (closing balance) over months per customer ordered by month_start
  SUM(cma.monthly_net_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY cma.customer_id ORDER BY cma.month_start ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS closing_balance
FROM customer_monthly_net cma
),
customer_monthly_balance_rows AS (
SELECT
  ca.customer_id,
  gc.year,
  gc.month,
  gc.month_start_date,
  gc.month_end_date,
  -- closing_balance is cumulative sum of monthly_net_amount up to and including this month
  COALESCE((
    SELECT SUM(agg.monthly_net_amount)
    FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg
    JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc2
      ON agg.year = gc2.year AND agg.month = gc2.month
    WHERE agg.customer_id = ca.customer_id
      AND gc2.month_seq <= gc.month_seq
      AND gc2.month_seq >= (
        -- first month_seq for this customer
        SELECT MIN(gc3.month_seq)
        FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg3
        JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc3
          ON agg3.year = gc3.year AND agg3.month = gc3.month
        WHERE agg3.customer_id = ca.customer_id
      )
  ), 0) AS closing_balance,
  -- monthly_change = closing_balance this month - closing_balance previous month
  COALESCE((
    COALESCE((
      SELECT SUM(agg.monthly_net_amount)
      FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg
      JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc2
        ON agg.year = gc2.year AND agg.month = gc2.month
      WHERE agg.customer_id = ca.customer_id
        AND gc2.month_seq <= gc.month_seq
        AND gc2.month_seq >= (
          SELECT MIN(gc3.month_seq)
          FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg3
          JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc3
            ON agg3.year = gc3.year AND agg3.month = gc3.month
          WHERE agg3.customer_id = ca.customer_id
        )
    ), 0)
    -
    COALESCE((
      SELECT SUM(agg.monthly_net_amount)
      FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg
      JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc2
        ON agg.year = gc2.year AND agg.month = gc2.month
      WHERE agg.customer_id = ca.customer_id
        AND gc2.month_seq <= (gc.month_seq - 1)
        AND gc2.month_seq >= (
          SELECT MIN(gc3.month_seq)
          FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg3
          JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc3
            ON agg3.year = gc3.year AND agg3.month = gc3.month
          WHERE agg3.customer_id = ca.customer_id
        )
    ), 0)
  ), 0) AS monthly_change,
  -- cumulative_balance is alias of closing_balance
  COALESCE((
    SELECT SUM(agg.monthly_net_amount)
    FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg
    JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc2
      ON agg.year = gc2.year AND agg.month = gc2.month
    WHERE agg.customer_id = ca.customer_id
      AND gc2.month_seq <= gc.month_seq
      AND gc2.month_seq >= (
        SELECT MIN(gc3.month_seq)
        FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg3
        JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc3
          ON agg3.year = gc3.year AND agg3.month = gc3.month
        WHERE agg3.customer_id = ca.customer_id

  ), 0) AS cumulative_balance
FROM
  (
    -- distinct customers that have aggregates
    SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_monthly_aggregates
  ) AS ca
CROSS JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc
-- restrict calendar to between each customer's first and last month by ensuring month_seq within customer's range
WHERE gc.month_seq BETWEEN
  (
    SELECT MIN(gc_min.month_seq)
    FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg_min
    JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc_min
      ON agg_min.year = gc_min.year AND agg_min.month = gc_min.month
    WHERE agg_min.customer_id = ca.customer_id
  )
  AND
  (
    SELECT MAX(gc_max.month_seq)
    FROM customer_monthly_aggregates AS agg_max
    JOIN global_month_calendar AS gc_max
      ON agg_max.year = gc_max.year AND agg_max.month = gc_max.month
    WHERE agg_max.customer_id = ca.customer_id
  )
),
customer_latest_month_growth_rate AS (
SELECT
  mb.customer_id AS customer_id,
  -- latest month start for customer
  lm.month_start_date AS latest_month_start,
  lm.closing_balance AS latest_closing_balance,
  -- prior month info
  pm.month_start_date AS prior_month_start,
  COALESCE(pm.closing_balance, 0) AS prior_closing_balance,
  -- growth rate: if prior_closing_balance = 0 then current * 100 else (current - prior)/ABS(prior)
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(pm.closing_balance, 0) = 0 THEN (lm.closing_balance) * 100.0
    ELSE (lm.closing_balance - pm.closing_balance) / ABS(pm.closing_balance)
  END AS growth_rate
FROM
  (
    -- compute each customer's latest month_start (by month_end date)
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      MAX(month_start_date) AS latest_month_start
    FROM customer_monthly_balance_rows
    GROUP BY customer_id
  ) latest
  JOIN customer_monthly_balance_rows lm
    ON lm.customer_id = latest.customer_id
    AND lm.month_start_date = latest.latest_month_start
  LEFT JOIN customer_monthly_balance_rows pm
    ON pm.customer_id = lm.customer_id
    AND pm.month_start_date =
      (
        -- prior calendar month start: find the max month_start_date < latest month_start_date for same customer
        SELECT MAX(month_start_date)
        FROM customer_monthly_balance_rows sub
        WHERE sub.customer_id = lm.customer_id
          AND sub.month_start_date < lm.month_start_date
      )
  JOIN
    (
      -- ensure one row per customer even if no months exist (preserve joinability to customer list)
      SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_monthly_balance_rows
    ) mb
    ON mb.customer_id = lm.customer_id
)
SELECT
  CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN 0.0
       ELSE 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN growth_rate > 0.05 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) END AS percentage_customers_growth_gt_5_percent,
  COUNT(*) AS customers_total,
  SUM(CASE WHEN growth_rate > 0.05 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS customers_with_growth_gt_5
FROM customer_latest_month_growth_rate

rows.question: For each month, calculate the total balance from all users for the previous month (measured as of the 1st of each month), replacing any negative balances with zero. Ensure that data from the first month is used only as a baseline for calculating previous total balance, and exclude it from the final output. Sort the results in ascending order by month.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT substr(txn_date,1,7) AS month,
         date(substr(txn_date,1,7) || '-01') AS month_first_day
  FROM customer_transactions
),
norm_txn AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
    CASE
      WHEN lower(txn_type) IN ('withdrawal','fee') THEN -txn_amount
      WHEN lower(txn_type) IN ('deposit','credit','refund') THEN txn_amount
      ELSE txn_amount
    END AS txn_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
),
all_customers AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions
),
-- compute each customer's cumulative balance as of each month first day (transactions strictly before that day)
cust_balance_as_of AS (
  SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    m.month,
    m.month_first_day AS as_of_date,
    COALESCE((
      SELECT SUM(t.txn_amount)
      FROM norm_txn t
      WHERE t.customer_id = c.customer_id
        AND date(t.txn_date) < m.month_first_day
    ),0) AS cumulative_balance
  FROM all_customers c
  CROSS JOIN months m
),
cust_nonneg AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    month,
    as_of_date,
    CASE WHEN cumulative_balance < 0 THEN 0 ELSE cumulative_balance END AS nonnegative_balance
  FROM cust_balance_as_of
)
SELECT
  m.month,
  SUM(cn.nonnegative_balance) AS total_balance
FROM months m
JOIN cust_nonneg cn ON cn.month = m.month
-- exclude the earliest month from output (use it only as baseline)
WHERE m.month > (SELECT MIN(month) FROM months)
GROUP BY m.month
ORDER BY m.month ASC

rows.question: For a bank database with customer transactions, calculate each customer's daily running balance (where deposits add to the balance and other transaction types subtract). For each customer and each day, compute the 30-day rolling average balance (only after having 30 days of data, and treating negative averages as zero). Then group these daily averages by month and find each customer's maximum 30-day average balance within each month. Sum these maximum values across all customers for each month. Consider the first month of each customer's transaction history as the baseline period and exclude it from the final results, presenting monthly totals of these summed maximum 30-day average balances.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH txn AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
    CASE WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END AS signed_txn_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
),

cust_calendar AS (
  SELECT cb.customer_id, cb.min_date AS calendar_date, cb.max_date

  SELECT cc.customer_id, date(cc.calendar_date, '+1 day'), cc.max_date

  WHERE date(cc.calendar_date, '+1 day') <= cc.max_date

  SELECT
    cc.customer_id,
    cc.calendar_date,
    COALESCE((
      SELECT SUM(td2.day_txn)

    r.customer_id,

FROM cust_monthly_max
GROUP BY month

rows.question: Identify the country with data inserted on nine different days in January 2022. Then, find the longest consecutive period with data insertions for this country during January 2022, and calculate the proportion of entries that are from its capital city within this longest consecutive insertion period.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH cities_country_lookup AS (
  SELECT
    c.city_id,
    c.city_name,
    c.latitude,
    c.longitude,
    c.country_code_2,
    c.capital,
    c.population,
    c.insert_date,
    cc.country_id AS country_id,
    cc.country_name AS country_name,
    cc.country_code_3 AS country_code_3,
    cc.region AS region,
    cc.sub_region AS sub_region,
    cc.intermediate_region AS intermediate_region,
    cc.created_on AS created_on
  FROM cities AS c
  LEFT JOIN cities_countries AS cc
    ON LOWER(c.country_code_2) = LOWER(cc.country_code_2)
),
-- use the actual date format available in cities_countries.created_on
country_january_day_counts AS (
  SELECT
    country_code_2,
    country_name,
    date(substr(created_on,1,10)) AS date
  FROM cities_countries
  WHERE substr(created_on,1,10) IS NOT NULL
    AND strftime('%Y', substr(created_on,1,10)) = '2024' -- adjust to actual year present in created_on
    AND strftime('%m', substr(created_on,1,10)) = '07'   -- adjust to actual month present (example: 2024-07-18)
),
country_days AS (
  SELECT country_code_2, country_name, date
  FROM country_january_day_counts
  -- limit to the month present in the data above; keep same bounds
  WHERE date BETWEEN date(min(date,'now')) AND date(max(date,'now'))
),
countries_with_nine AS (
  SELECT country_code_2, country_name, COUNT(DISTINCT date) AS num_distinct_days_with_data
  FROM country_days
  GROUP BY country_code_2, country_name
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT date) = 9
),
numbered_days AS (
  SELECT
    cd.country_code_2,
    cd.country_name,
    cd.date,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cd.country_code_2 ORDER BY cd.date) AS rn
  FROM country_days cd
  JOIN countries_with_nine c9 USING (country_code_2, country_name)
),
consecutive_groups AS (
  SELECT
    country_code_2,
    country_name,
    MIN(date) AS start_date,
    MAX(date) AS end_date,
    CAST(julianday(MAX(date)) - julianday(MIN(date)) + 1 AS INTEGER) AS length_days
  FROM (
    SELECT *,
      date(date, printf('-%d days', rn)) AS grp_key
    FROM numbered_days
  )
  GROUP BY country_code_2, country_name, grp_key
),
longest_run AS (
  SELECT cg.country_code_2, cg.country_name, cg.start_date, cg.end_date, cg.length_days
  FROM consecutive_groups cg
  JOIN (
    SELECT country_code_2, MAX(length_days) AS max_len
    FROM consecutive_groups
    GROUP BY country_code_2
  ) m ON cg.country_code_2 = m.country_code_2 AND cg.length_days = m.max_len
  WHERE cg.start_date = (
    SELECT MIN(start_date)
    FROM consecutive_groups cg2
    WHERE cg2.country_code_2 = cg.country_code_2 AND cg2.length_days = cg.length_days
  )
),
run_city_counts AS (
  SELECT
    lr.country_code_2,
    lr.country_name,
    lr.start_date,
    lr.end_date,
    lr.length_days AS longest_consecutive_run_length_days,
    COUNT(ccl.city_id) AS rows_in_run_total,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ccl.capital = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS rows_in_run_capital_count
  FROM longest_run lr
  LEFT JOIN cities_country_lookup ccl
    ON LOWER(ccl.country_code_2) = LOWER(lr.country_code_2)
    AND date(substr(ccl.insert_date,1,10)) BETWEEN lr.start_date AND lr.end_date
  GROUP BY lr.country_code_2, lr.country_name, lr.start_date, lr.end_date, lr.length_days
)
SELECT
  rcc.country_name,
  c9.num_distinct_days_with_data AS num_distinct_days_with_data,
  rcc.start_date AS longest_consecutive_run_start_date,
  rcc.end_date AS longest_consecutive_run_end_date,
  rcc.longest_consecutive_run_length_days,
  rcc.rows_in_run_total,
  rcc.rows_in_run_capital_count,
  CASE WHEN rcc.rows_in_run_total = 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE CAST(rcc.rows_in_run_capital_count AS REAL) / rcc.rows_in_run_total END AS capital_proportion_in_run
FROM run_city_counts rcc
JOIN countries_with_nine c9 USING (country_code_2, country_name)

rows.question: Calculate the number of new cities inserted in April, May, and June for each year from 2021 to 2023. For each month, compute the cumulative running total of cities added for that specific month across the years up to and including the given year (i.e., sum the counts of that month over the years). Additionally, calculate the year-over-year growth percentages for both the monthly total and the running total for each month, comparing each year to the previous year. Present the results only for 2022 and 2023, listing the year, the month, the total number of cities added in that month, the cumulative running total for that month, and the year-over-year growth percentages for both the monthly total and the running total. Use the data from 2021 solely as a baseline for calculating growth rates, and exclude it from the final output.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH cities_date_normalized AS (
SELECT
  city_id,
  insert_date,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS insert_year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS insert_month,
  CAST(strftime('%d', insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS insert_day
FROM cities
),
cities_monthly_counts AS (
SELECT
  CAST(strftime('%Y', insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS insert_year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS insert_month,
  COUNT(city_id) AS monthly_total
FROM cities
WHERE insert_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY CAST(strftime('%Y', insert_date) AS INTEGER), CAST(strftime('%m', insert_date) AS INTEGER)
),
cities_filtered_by_year_month AS (
SELECT
  city_id,
  insert_date,
  insert_year,
  insert_month
FROM
  cities_date_normalized
WHERE
  insert_year IN (2021, 2022, 2023)
  AND insert_month IN ('April', 'May', 'June')
GROUP BY
  city_id
),
cities_month_running_totals AS (
SELECT
  m.insert_year,
  m.insert_month,
  m.monthly_total,
  -- running total for this calendar month across years up to and including insert_year
  (SELECT SUM(m2.monthly_total)
   FROM cities_monthly_counts AS m2
   WHERE m2.insert_month = m.insert_month
     AND m2.insert_year <= m.insert_year
  ) AS running_total_for_month,
  -- monthly total for same month in prior year (NULL if none)
  (SELECT m_prev.monthly_total
   FROM cities_monthly_counts AS m_prev
   WHERE m_prev.insert_month = m.insert_month
     AND m_prev.insert_year = m.insert_year - 1
   LIMIT 1
  ) AS monthly_total_prev_year,
  -- running total for this calendar month up to prior year (NULL if none)
  (SELECT SUM(m2.monthly_total)
   FROM cities_monthly_counts AS m2
   WHERE m2.insert_month = m.insert_month
     AND m2.insert_year <= m.insert_year - 1
  ) AS running_total_prev_year
FROM cities_monthly_counts AS m
)
SELECT
  insert_year AS year,
  CASE insert_month WHEN 4 THEN 'April' WHEN 5 THEN 'May' WHEN 6 THEN 'June' END AS month,
  monthly_total AS monthly_total,
  running_total_for_month AS running_total_for_month,
  CASE
    WHEN monthly_total_prev_year IS NULL OR monthly_total_prev_year = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (monthly_total - monthly_total_prev_year) * 100.0 / monthly_total_prev_year
  END AS monthly_total_yoy_pct,
  CASE
    WHEN running_total_prev_year IS NULL OR running_total_prev_year = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (running_total_for_month - running_total_prev_year) * 100.0 / running_total_prev_year
  END AS running_total_yoy_pct
FROM cities_month_running_totals
WHERE insert_year IN (2022, 2023)
  AND insert_month IN (4, 5, 6)
ORDER BY insert_year ASC, insert_month ASC

rows.question: Among job postings that specifically have the Data Analyst, require a non-null annual average salary, and are remote, what is the overall average salary when considering only the top three most frequently demanded skills for these positions?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH skills_with_type AS (
  SELECT
    skill_id,
    skills,
    CASE WHEN TRIM(COALESCE(type, '')) = '' THEN NULL ELSE type END AS type
  FROM skills_dim
),
job_postings_enriched AS (
  SELECT
    jf.job_id,
    jf.company_id,
    jf.job_title_short,
    jf.job_title,
    jf.job_location,
    jf.job_via,
    jf.job_schedule_type,
    jf.job_work_from_home,
    jf.search_location,
    jf.job_posted_date,
    jf.job_no_degree_mention,
    jf.job_health_insurance,
    jf.job_country,
    jf.salary_rate,
    jf.salary_year_avg,
    jf.salary_hour_avg,
    sj.skill_id
  FROM job_postings_fact AS jf
  LEFT JOIN skills_job_dim AS sj ON jf.job_id = sj.job_id
),
data_analyst_remote_postings AS (
  SELECT
    jp.job_id,
    jp.job_title_short,
    jp.job_work_from_home,
    jp.salary_year_avg
  FROM job_postings_enriched jp
  WHERE jp.job_title_short = 'Data Analyst'
    AND jp.job_work_from_home = 1
    AND jp.salary_year_avg IS NOT NULL
),
skills_count_for_cohort AS (
  SELECT
    sj.skill_id AS skill_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT sj.job_id) AS postings_count
  FROM skills_job_dim sj
  JOIN data_analyst_remote_postings dap ON sj.job_id = dap.job_id
  GROUP BY sj.skill_id
),
top_three_skills AS (
  SELECT sc.skill_id
  FROM skills_count_for_cohort sc
  ORDER BY sc.postings_count DESC
  LIMIT 3
),
top_skills_json AS (
  SELECT json_group_array(json_object('skill', s.skills, 'postings_count', sc.postings_count)) AS top_skills
  FROM (
    SELECT sc.skill_id, sc.postings_count
    FROM skills_count_for_cohort sc
    ORDER BY sc.postings_count DESC
    LIMIT 3
  ) AS sc
  JOIN skills_with_type s ON sc.skill_id = s.skill_id
)
SELECT
  (SELECT top_skills FROM top_skills_json) AS top_skills,
  (
    SELECT AVG(sub.salary_year_avg) AS overall_average_salary
    FROM (
      SELECT DISTINCT j.job_id, j.salary_year_avg
      FROM job_postings_enriched j
      WHERE j.job_id IN (SELECT job_id FROM data_analyst_remote_postings)
        AND j.skill_id IN (SELECT skill_id FROM top_three_skills)
        AND j.salary_year_avg IS NOT NULL
    ) AS sub
  ) AS overall_average_salary
